attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content: {"result":"{\"success\": true, \"data\": {\"path\": \"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_4/projects/trace-verdict-study/paper_framing.md\", \"content\": \"# Paper Framing — trace-verdict-study\\n\\n> v2.4 — [UPDATED 2026-05-15] 修正 calibration 比值用精确值计算 (~63x ECE, ~150x Brier)；加入完整 calibration 数据 + seed robustness 证据最终整合。\\n\\n## Target Venue\\n- Primary: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR submission)\\n- Fallback: EMNLP 2026 Findings\\n- Deadline: ARR May 25, 2026\\n\\n## Core Insight\\n\\nVerdict prediction (pass/fail) is fundamentally a **fault detection** task. The minimal sufficient signal is the **exception event** — a compact, structured diagnostic moment that achieves near-perfect accuracy (Qwen 99.83%, DeepSeek 99.33%, cross-model gap = 0.50pp) regardless of model architecture. In contrast, richer trace representations that require deeper execution reasoning show model-dependent effectiveness: VOTA gap = 14.96pp, no_trace gap = 1.77pp. Information density — not training signal distribution — is the primary bottleneck: even oracle loss masking (label-only) cannot close the 13pp gap between full traces and targeted extraction. The design principle: **extract the highest-specificity diagnostic signal; discard everything else.**\\n\\n## Core Claims (3)\\n\\n### Claim 1: Exception-based fault detection is model-agnostic\\n\\nException summaries alone achieve near-perfect verdict prediction across architecturally distinct models: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B (99.83%) and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B (99.33%), cross-model gap = 0.50pp (at best checkpoint, gap = 0pp). This contrasts with VOTA (gap = 14.96pp) and no_trace (gap = 1.77pp). Exception events are structurally simple (`[ERROR] type: ... message: ...`) and do not require deep trace reasoning — making them universally extractable.\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`: Qwen 99.83%\\n- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: DeepSeek 99.33% (epoch3) / 99.83% (epoch1 best)\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: DeepSeek VOTA 84.45% (gap = 14.96pp)\\n- `deepseek_no_trace_seed42`: DeepSeek no_trace 73.36% (gap = 1.77pp)\\n- `vota_no_ae_seed42`: 99.41% — actual/expected removal 不降，非 trivial string comparison\\n\\n**Seed robustness** [UPDATED 2026-05-15] ✅: Qwen exception_only 3-seed 完全一致，构成本文最强 robustness 证据：\\n\\n| Seed | Accuracy | 95% CI | Errors |\\n|------|----------|--------|--------|\\n| 42 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n| 123 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n| 456 | 99.83% | [99.58, 100] | 2/1190 |\\n\\n3 seeds 错误样本 100% 重叠（id=901, 905, 均为 `check_dict_case` 函数, label=pass → pred=fail）。**Irreducible samples**: 模型已达数据集理论上限，variance = 0。\\n\\n**DeepSeek cross-model**: epoch1 best checkpoint 99.83% 与 Qwen 完全一致（gap = 0pp），进一步确认 exception signal 的 universality。\\n\\n### Claim 2: Information density, not gradient dilution, drives trace compression benefit\\n\\nFull traces help verdict prediction (81.8%, +6.6pp over baseline), but VOTA achieves 99.41% (+24.3pp) — a +17.6pp advantage. Label-only loss ablation (plan_002) quantifies the causal decomposition: **gradient dilution contributes ~26% of the gap** (4.5pp; label-only full_trace = 86.2%), **information overload contributes ~74%** (13.0pp; only trace compression resolves this). Even with oracle loss masking that eliminates gradient dilution, full traces still underperform VOTA by 13pp.\\n\\nCross-model evidence reinforces this: VOTA gap (14.96pp) tracks base model execution reasoning capability (Qwen CRUXEval-I 56.5% vs DeepSeek 39.0%, Δ=17.5pp), suggesting trace utilization effectiveness is bounded by pretraining-derived inductive biases. Exception signal bypasses this bottleneck entirely (gap = 0.50pp).\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.2% (gradient dilution fix, +4.5pp over standard full_trace)\\n- `full_trace_seed42_v5`: 81.8% (standard full_trace)\\n- `vota_seed42_v5`: 99.41%\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (VOTA model-dependent)\\n- CRUXEval literature data (Wang et al.)\\n\\n### Claim 3: Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy for verdict prediction\\n\\nComponent ablation reveals verdict-relevant trace information has a strict two-tier hierarchy:\\n- **Tier 1 — diagnostic moment signals**: exception summaries (99.83%) and assertion-point information (99.92%) are individually near-perfect and sufficient for verdict prediction. These signals are structurally simple and model-agnostic (exception cross-model gap = 0.50pp).\\n- **Tier 2 — behavioral patterns**: loop compression (85.6%) carries substantial signal but is model-dependent and fully subsumed by Tier 1.\\n\\nCombining tiers introduces noise rather than helping: exception_only (99.83%) > VOTA full (99.41%), p=0.01. Loop_only ≈ full_trace_label_only (85.6% vs 86.2%) confirms VOTA's loop compression precisely extracts the useful behavioral signal from full traces.\\n\\n**Supporting evidence:**\\n- `vota_exception_only_seed42_v2`: 99.83% (Tier 1 exception)\\n- `vota_ae_only_seed42`: 99.92% (Tier 1 assertion-point, 与 exception 统计等价 p=0.80)\\n- `vota_loop_only_seed42`: 85.6% (Tier 2 behavioral)\\n- `full_trace_label_only_seed42`: 86.2% (≈ loop_only, confirming extraction equivalence)\\n- `deepseek_exception_only_seed42`: 99.33% (Tier 1 cross-model validation)\\n- `deepseek_vota_seed42`: 84.45% (Tier 1+2 cross-model: Tier 2 introduces model-dependent degradation)\\n\\n**Calibration** [UPDATED 2026-05-15]: 完整 calibration 数据确认 Tier 1 信号不仅 accuracy 近完美，置信度校准也近完美：\\n\\n| Condition | ECE | Brier | 解读 |\\n|-----------|-----|-------|------|\\n| ae_only | 0.0004 | 0.0008 | 近乎完美校准 |\\n| exception_only | 0.003 | 0.001 | 近乎完美校准 |\\n| VOTA | 0.005 | 0.005 | 优秀，但 Tier 2 引入轻微 noise |\\n| no_trace | 0.171 | 0.197 | 严重 miscalibrated |\\n\\nno_trace ECE 是 exception_only 的 **~63x**（0.1715/0.0027），Brier 是 **~150x**（0.1972/0.0013）。Trace signal（尤其 Tier 1）不仅提升 accuracy，更从根本上改善模型 calibration。no_trace 的高 Brier score (0.197) 表明模型在无 trace 时不仅 accuracy 低，且对错误预测过度自信。\\n\\n**Design principle**: verdict-optimized traces should extract highest-specificity diagnostic signals; lower-specificity signals are redundant and may introduce noise.\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n- **Problem**: Existing trace SFT studies (DCSH, TracePile) evaluate only generative tasks and find limited, model-dependent benefit. No prior work has tested trace SFT on verdict tasks (binary pass/fail), nor identified what trace components drive classification performance.\\n\\n- **Existing approaches & gaps**: DCSH (EMNLP Findings 2025) tested 5 trace formats on generation tasks, finding that \\\"no single trace representation consistently outperforms others.\\\" TracePile (NeurIPS 2025) scaled to 2.6M samples but only evaluated generation. TRACED (ICSE 2024) showed traces help encoder-based classification. All existing trace formats are designed for execution simulation, not fault detection.\\n\\n- **Our framing**: We reframe verdict prediction as **fault detection** and ask: what is the minimal sufficient diagnostic signal? Through systematic component ablation across two architecturally distinct models, we discover that exception events — compact, structured error summaries — are both necessary and sufficient, achieving near-perfect accuracy (99.5%+ avg) with near-zero cross-model gap. Richer trace representations work only when the base model has sufficient execution reasoning capability, making them unreliable for general deployment.\\n\\n- **Headline result**: \\\"Exception-based trace SFT achieves 99.83% verdict accuracy on Qwen and 99.33% on DeepSeek (gap = 0.50pp), while the same models show a 14.96pp gap on VOTA traces — demonstrating that fault detection, not trace reasoning, is the robust mechanism for verdict prediction.\\\"\\n\\n## Story Arc\\n\\n1. **Setup**: Trace SFT for code tasks — promising but inconsistent in prior work (DCSH, TracePile). Unknown whether traces help verdict tasks and what trace design matters.\\n\\n2. **First result — traces help, compression helps more** (single model): no_trace 75.1% → full_trace 81.8% → VOTA 99.41%. Label-only loss ablation decomposes the gap: 26% gradient dilution, 74% information overload. Compression improves accuracy through higher information density, not just cost savings.\\n\\n3. **Twist — what component actually drives VOTA?** Component ablation reveals exception_only (99.83%) ≥ full VOTA (99.41%). The \\\"trace reasoning\\\" narrative is wrong — verdict prediction is fault detection. Tier 1 (exceptions + assertion-point) subsumes Tier 2 (loops). Actual/expected removal doesn't hurt (99.41%).\\n\\n4. **Cross-model stress test — the universal vs the contingent**: Exception_only transfers with near-zero gap (0.50pp), but VOTA degrades by 14.96pp on DeepSeek. The model-agnostic component is precisely the one that doesn't require trace reasoning. CRUXEval reasoning gap (17.5pp) parallels VOTA gap — trace utilization is bounded by pretraining. [UPDATED 2026-05-15] Seed robustness (3-seed variance = 0) + calibration (ECE=0.003) 双重确认 exception signal 的 reliability。\\n\\n5. **Design principle**: For verdict tasks, identify the highest-specificity diagnostic signal (exception events) and discard everything else. Simpler signals are more robust; complexity tolerance depends on model capability.\\n\\n## DeepSeek full_trace 处理\\n\\n**现状**: v1 坍塌（28.5%, 100% 预测 fail, 根因: 训练端 label 截断）。v2 重训启动但被 kill（Loop #6 ops worker 腾 GPU 给 vota_seed456）。\\n\\n**处理方案**: 下一个 GPU 空闲（deepseek_exception_only_seed123 完成后 ~20:15 UTC）立即重启 deepseek_full_trace_v3。\\n\\n**对论文叙事的影响**: 无. 三个有效条件 (exception_only, VOTA, no_trace) 已足够支撑全部 claims. DeepSeek full_trace 结果是 bonus, 非必需. 若 v3 在投稿前完成, 纳入跨模型对比表 (4/4 conditions). 否则报告为 N/A 并在 Limitations 中透明披露根因.\\n\\n## Venue Fit Risks\\n\\n| Risk | Assessment | Mitigation |\\n|------|-----------|------------|\\n| 单任务 | 仍然只在 test verdict prediction 上验证 | 跨模型验证部分弥补; Discussion 中讨论 generalization |\\n| 单数据集 | CRUXEval 是唯一 benchmark | 定位为 empirical study, 深度优于广度 |\\n| \\\"只是 feature engineering\\\" | exception extraction 不复杂 | simplicity 本身是 contribution — 最简信号最 robust |\\n| Negative result 味道 | VOTA 跨模型不 robust | Reframe: 识别 robust vs non-robust 组件边界是 positive |\\n| Seed robustness | ✅ 已解决: 99.83% ± 0.00 (3 seeds), irreducible samples 确认 | — |\\n| Calibration | [UPDATED 2026-05-15] ✅ 完整数据: Tier 1 ECE≤0.003, no_trace ECE=0.171 (~63x gap) | Brier ~150x gap 进一步确认 |\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n| Concern | Planned Response |\\n|---------|-----------------|\\n| \\\"exception_only 99.83% 是不是 trivial pattern matching [ERROR] 有无？\\\" | full_trace 也包含 [ERROR] 但仅 81.8%——模型需要从 trace context 中 extract 和 utilize exception signal, 不是简单 keyword detection. no_trace 无 exception, 75.1%. |\\n| \\\"为什么 exception_only > VOTA? adding info 反而降?\\\" | 非 exception 组件 (loop/ae tokens) 稀释 attention 对 exception 信号的聚焦. Calibration: exception_only ECE=0.003 vs VOTA ECE=0.005. 部分样本 loop 正常但有 exception, 引入矛盾信号. |\\n| \\\"CRUXEval gap 与 VOTA gap 的相关性可能是 coincidence\\\" | 明确标注为 hypothesis. 列出 alternatives (tokenizer efficiency, pretraining scale 2.75x, chat template). 不 overclaim. |\\n| \\\"只有 2 个模型\\\" | 同意是 limitation. 两模型在 architecture, pretraining data (5.5T vs 2T), execution reasoning (CRUXEval 17.5pp gap) 上有充分差异, 不是 trivial replication. |\\n| \\\"99.83% 可能 saturated, 看不出 exception 到底学了什么\\\" | [UPDATED 2026-05-15] Calibration 双指标: exception_only ECE=0.003, Brier=0.001 (近完美校准). 对比 no_trace ECE=0.171, Brier=0.197 (~63x/~150x gap). Irreducible samples (id=901,905) 分析说明模型已达数据上限. |\\n| \\\"只用了 1 个 seed\\\" | ✅ 已解决: 3 seeds 结果完全一致 (99.83% ± 0.00), irreducible samples 100% 重叠, 95% CI 均为 [99.58, 100]. |\\n| \\\"eval_loss 上升但 accuracy 提升——checkpoint selection 有问题?\\\" | Discussion: token-level loss 与 binary verdict accuracy 解耦. 推荐 verdict-specific metric. Methodological contribution. |\\n| \\\"DeepSeek full_trace 坍塌是 bug 不是 finding\\\" | 诚实披露根因 (训练端 label 截断). 其他 3 条件不受影响. 修复版本如就绪则补入. |\\n| \\\"calibration 数据只有 1 个 seed\\\" | [UPDATED 2026-05-15] Seed robustness 已证明 accuracy variance=0 (3 seeds), calibration 在 accuracy 完全一致的前提下 expected 也一致. ECE/Brier 的极小值 (0.003/0.001) 留有极小 variance 空间. |\\n\\n## Discussion 要点\\n\\n### D1: eval_loss vs verdict accuracy 解耦\\nDeepSeek VOTA: eval_loss epoch1→3 从 0.068 升至 0.112 (+65%), 但 accuracy 从 78.15% 升至 84.45% (+6.3pp). Token-level calibration 与 binary classification accuracy 方向相反. **Implication**: verdict tasks 应用 task-specific metric (accuracy/F1) 做 checkpoint selection, 非 eval_loss.\\n\\n### D2: CRUXEval gap 假说\\nVOTA 跨模型 gap (14.96pp) 与 CRUXEval execution reasoning gap (15-17.5pp) 数值吻合. 假说: trace utilization effectiveness 受 base model \\\"execution reasoning readiness\\\" 约束. **标注**: hypothesis, N=2, 列出 alternatives. 不 overclaim.\\n\\n### D3: Simplicity as robustness\\nException signal 跨模型 robust 恰因其 structurally simple. 暗示 **trace design 应匹配 deployment model 的能力下界**, 而非上界.\\n\\n### D4: Checkpoint selection 与 gap 报告\\n正文 exception_only 跨模型 gap 用 final-to-final = 0.50pp (一致 criterion). 补充: at best checkpoint (DeepSeek epoch1), gap = 0pp. DeepSeek epoch1→3 退化 0.50pp 与 D1 eval_loss 解耦现象一致.\\n\\n### D5: Irreducible samples\\n3 seeds 的 2/1190 errors 完全相同（id=901, 905, `check_dict_case`），方向一致（pass→fail false negatives）。模型已达数据集理论上限。这些样本可能存在 labeling noise 或 edge-case 行为（exception trace 中缺少足够的 fault signal）。\\n\\n### D6: Calibration as secondary evidence [UPDATED 2026-05-15]\\nCalibration 数据提供独立于 accuracy 的 evidence dimension。no_trace Brier=0.197 说明模型无 trace 时不仅预测错，且对错误预测过度自信。exception_only Brier=0.001 说明模型在有 exception signal 时几乎完美区分确定性和不确定性。这支持 Claim 1 的 \\\"sufficient signal\\\" 论点——exception 不仅让模型预测对，还让模型 \\\"知道自己对\\\"。\\n\\n## Contingency Framing (已解决, 留存档)\\n\\n### Claim 1 — RESOLVED (D008 → D010 → D019)\\nvota_no_ae 99.41% 否定 trivial comparison. exception_only 99.83% 揭示核心机制. 跨模型 0.50pp gap 确认 universality.\\n\\n### Claim 2 — RESOLVED (D006 + D009)\\nv5 full_trace 81.8%. plan_002 label-only 86.2%, gradient dilution = minor (26%). 跨模型 VOTA gap 补充证据.\\n\\n## 与 v1 Framing 的关键差异\\n\\n| 维度 | v1 | v2.3 |\\n|------|----|----|\\n| Headline | VOTA compression 优于 full trace | Exception-based fault detection is model-agnostic |\\n| Primary claim | VOTA +24pp through fault indicator preservation | Exception signal transfers across models (gap = 0.50pp) |\\n| Claim 2 | Compression > full trace (只有 gradient dilution) | Information density primary + gradient dilution quantification + cross-model reinforcement |\\n| Claim 3 Tier 1 | exception_only only | exception + assertion-point (co-Tier 1, D020) |\\n| Model scope | 单模型 (Qwen) | 双模型, 跨模型对比是核心贡献 |\\n| VOTA 定位 | 核心方法 | Model-dependent richer representation |\\n| DeepSeek no_trace 对比确认 trace 的 calibration 价值 |\\n\", \"total_chars\": 14205, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Core Claims (3)

**对论文叙事的影响**: 无. 三个有效条件 (exception_only, VOTA, no_trace) 已足够支撑全部 claims. DeepSeek full_trace 结果是 bonus, 非必需. 若 v3 在投稿前完成, 纳入跨模型对比表 (4/4 conditions). 否则报告为 N/A 并在 Limitations 中透明披露根因.

## Venue Fit Risks

| Risk | Assessment | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|------------|
| 单任务 | 仍然只在 test verdict prediction 上验证 | 跨模型验证部分弥补; Discussion 中讨论 generalization |
| 单数据集 | CRUXEval 是唯一 benchmark | 定位为 empirical study, 深度优于广度 |
| "只是 feature engineering" | exception extraction 不复杂 | simplicity 本身是 contribution — 最简信号最 robust |
| Negative result 味道 | VOTA 跨模型不 robust | Reframe: 识别 robust vs non-robust 组件边界是 positive |
| Seed robustness | ✅ 已解决: 99.83% ± 0.00 (3 seeds), irreducible samples 确认 | — |
| Calibration | [UPDATED 2026-05-15] ✅ 完整数据: Tier 1 ECE≤0.003, no_trace ECE=0.171 (~63x gap) | Brier ~150x gap 进一步确认 |

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

| Concern | Planned Response |
|---------|-----------------|
| "exception_only 99.83% 是不是 trivial pattern matching [ERROR] 有无？" | full_trace 也包含 [ERROR] 但仅 81.8%——模型需要从 trace context 中 extract 和 utilize exception signal, 不是简单 keyword detection. no_trace 无 exception, 75.1%. |
| "为什么 exception_only > VOTA? adding info 反而降?" | 非 exception 组件 (loop/ae tokens) 稀释 attention 对 exception 信号的聚焦. Calibration: exception_only ECE=0.003 vs VOTA ECE=0.005. 部分样本 loop 正常但有 exception, 引入矛盾信号. |
| "CRUXEval gap 与 VOTA gap 的相关性可能是 coincidence" | 明确标注为 hypothesis. 列出 alternatives (tokenizer efficiency, pretraining scale 2.75x, chat template). 不 overclaim. |
| "只有 2 个模型" | 同意是 limitation. 两模型在 architecture, pretraining data (5.5T vs 2T), execution reasoning (CRUXEval 17.5pp gap) 上有充分差异, 不是 trivial replication. |
| "99.83% 可能 saturated, 看不出 exception 到底学了什么" | [UPDATED 2026-05-15] Calibration 双指标: exception_only ECE=0.003, Brier=0.001 (近完美校准). 对比 no_trace ECE=0.171, Brier=0.197 (~63x/~150x gap). Irreducible samples (id=901,905) 分析说明模型已达数据上限. |
| "只用了 1 个 seed" | ✅ 已解决: 3 seeds 结果完全一致 (99.83% ± 0.00), irreducible samples 100% 重叠, 95% CI 均为 [99.58, 100]. |

### D1: eval_loss vs verdict accuracy 解耦
DeepSeek VOTA: eval_loss epoch1→3 从 0.068 升至 0.112 (+65%), 但 accuracy 从 78.15% 升至 84.45% (+6.3pp). Token-level calibration 与 binary classification accuracy 方向相反. **Implication**: verdict tasks 应用 task-specific metric (accuracy/F1) 做 checkpoint selection, 非 eval_loss.

### D2: CRUXEval gap 假说
VOTA 跨模型 gap (14.96pp) 与 CRUXEval execution reasoning gap (15-17.5pp) 数值吻合. 假说: trace utilization effectiveness 受 base model "execution reasoning readiness" 约束. **标注**: hypothesis, N=2, 列出 alternatives. 不 overclaim.

### D3: Simplicity as robustness
Exception signal 跨模型 robust 恰因其 structurally simple. 暗示 **trace design 应匹配 deployment model 的能力下界**, 而非上界.

### D4: Checkpoint selection 与 gap 报告
正文 exception_only 跨模型 gap 用 final-to-final = 0.50pp (一致 criterion). 补充: at best checkpoint (DeepSeek epoch1), gap = 0pp. DeepSeek epoch1→3 退化 0.50pp 与 D1 eval_loss 解耦现象一致.

### D6: Calibration as secondary evidence [UPDATED 2026-05-15]
Calibration 数据提供独立于 accuracy 的 evidence dimension。no_trace Brier=0.197 说明模型无 trace 时不仅预测错，且对错误预测过度自信。exception_only Brier=0.001 说明模型在有 exception signal 时几乎完美区分确定性和不确定性。这支持 Claim 1 的 "sufficient signal" 论点——exception 不仅让模型预测对，还让模型 "知道自己对"。

1	\section{Discussion}
2	
3	\subsection{Why Exception Events Dominate}
4	
5	Verdict prediction is fundamentally a fault detection task: the model must determine whether execution deviated from expected behavior.
6	Exception events are the most explicit signal of such deviation---structured diagnostic moments that encode the nature and location of a fault.
7	Unlike loop compressions or assertion-point values, which require the model to integrate information across multiple trace elements, exception events provide a self-contained verdict cue.
8	This explains why \texttt{exception\_only} matches or exceeds VOTA: adding non-exception trace components dilutes the model's attention on the diagnostic signal rather than providing complementary information.
9	
10	We acknowledge that exception-based verdict prediction is, at its core, fault indicator presence detection: the model learns to map the presence or absence of a structured error message to a binary label, which is close to trivially solvable for any instruction-tuned LLM.
11	The Tier~1 accuracy of ${\geq}$99.8\% is therefore unsurprising in isolation.
12	The contribution of this finding lies not in demonstrating that a strong signal yields high accuracy, but in two less obvious results: (a)~adding more trace information---loop compressions, assertion-point values---actively \emph{hurts} performance (VOTA $<$ \texttt{exception\_only}, Table~\ref{tab:ablation}), quantifying an information density dilution effect that has not been previously measured; and (b)~this dilution is model-dependent, with DeepSeek VOTA fail recall collapsing to 45.43\% (Table~\ref{tab:per_class}) while Qwen maintains 100\%, revealing that mixed-signal trace processing amplifies capability gaps between models.
13	
14	\subsection{Simplicity as Robustness}
15	
16	The cross-model gap pattern (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a design principle: \emph{trace representations should match the model capability floor, not the ceiling.}
17	Exception events transfer across models precisely because they are structurally simple---a fixed-format error message that any instruction-tuned model can pattern-match.
18	VOTA's richer representation (loop summaries, assertion comparisons) requires compositional reasoning over heterogeneous formats, which the smaller DeepSeek model (2T pretrain tokens) cannot reliably perform---consistent with findings that SFT generalization depends heavily on base model capability \citep{yang2024generalization}.
19	The practical implication is that trace-based systems should default to the simplest sufficient signal, reserving richer representations for tasks that demonstrably require them.
20	
21	\subsection{Checkpoint Selection and Signal Stability}
22	
23	The DeepSeek \texttt{exception\_only} result reveals an instructive training dynamic: accuracy peaked at 99.83\% after epoch~1 but degraded to 99.33\% at convergence (epoch~3).
24	This 0.50pp drop means that the cross-model gap under \texttt{exception\_only} is 0pp at best checkpoint and 0.50pp at final checkpoint.
25	Both values are negligible, but the pattern has practical implications: continued training on a near-solved task can introduce overfitting to spurious correlations in the training set, degrading performance on the small number of ambiguous samples.
26	This is consistent with the observation that exception events provide such a strong signal that the model ``solves'' the task early; subsequent epochs optimize for marginal training loss reduction at the expense of generalization.
27	The contrast with VOTA is stark---DeepSeek VOTA accuracy does not exhibit this non-monotonic pattern, suggesting that the weaker model never fully learns the VOTA signal and thus does not overfit to it.
28	For deployment, this finding recommends early stopping or best-checkpoint selection when fine-tuning on high-signal trace conditions, rather than training to convergence.
29	
30	\subsection{Error Analysis}
31	\label{sec:error_analysis}
32	
33	Seed robustness testing revealed that the two errors made by \texttt{exception\_only} (accuracy = 99.83\%, 2/1190 incorrect) are \emph{identical across all three seeds} (42, 123, 456).
34	Both errors are false negatives on samples involving the \texttt{check\_dict\_case} function (sample IDs 901 and 905): the ground truth is \texttt{pass}, but the model predicts \texttt{fail}.
35	This 100\% error overlap ($\sigma{=}0$) across seeds demonstrates that these are not stochastic training artifacts but \emph{irreducible samples} at the boundary of what exception-based trace signals can resolve.
36	
37	We hypothesize that \texttt{check\_dict\_case} generates no exception events on passing inputs (correct behavior produces no errors), leaving the model without a distinguishing trace signal.
38	The model defaults to predicting \texttt{fail}---a reasonable heuristic when exception-based evidence is absent, since most trace-bearing inputs contain exception events precisely because they fail.
39	This systematic error pattern confirms that the two misclassifications represent a capability boundary of the exception-only format rather than a training instability, and that the 99.83\% accuracy is a deterministic ceiling for this trace representation on this dataset.
40	
41	\subsection{Limitations}
42	
43	Our study has several limitations.
44	First, all experiments use a single dataset derived from CRUXEval (800 Python functions); generalization to other languages, larger codebases, or different fault types remains untested.
45	Second, we evaluate only two models at the 7B parameter scale; the relationship between model size and trace signal utility is unexplored.
46	Third, the \texttt{exception\_only} seed robustness is confirmed (3 seeds, $\sigma{=}0$), but other conditions use a single seed.
47	Fourth, the DeepSeek \texttt{full\_trace} condition was invalidated because the DeepSeek tokenizer produced sequences exceeding 2,048 tokens, causing the verdict label to be truncated during training; the model consequently failed to learn the classification task, and we report it as N/A rather than presenting potentially misleading results.
48	Finally, our analysis is limited to verdict prediction; whether exception dominance extends to other classification tasks (vulnerability detection, clone detection) or to generation tasks (program repair) is an open question.

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{Why Exception Events Dominate}

Verdict prediction is fundamentally a fault detection task: the model must determine whether execution deviated from expected behavior.
Exception events are the most explicit signal of such deviation---structured diagnostic moments that encode the nature and location of a fault.
Unlike loop compressions or assertion-point values, which require the model to integrate information across multiple trace elements, exception events provide a self-contained verdict cue.
This explains why \texttt{exception\_only} matches or exceeds VOTA: adding non-exception trace components dilutes the model's attention on the diagnostic signal rather than providing complementary information.

We acknowledge that exception-based verdict prediction is, at its core, fault indicator presence detection: the model learns to map the presence or absence of a structured error message to a binary label, which is close to trivially solvable for any instruction-tuned LLM.
The Tier~1 accuracy of ${\geq}$99.8\% is therefore unsurprising in isolation.
The contribution of this finding lies not in demonstrating that a strong signal yields high accuracy, but in two less obvious results: (a)~adding more trace information---loop compressions, assertion-point values---actively \emph{hurts} performance (VOTA $<$ \texttt{exception\_only}, Table~\ref{tab:ablation}), quantifying an information density dilution effect that has not been previously measured; and (b)~this dilution is model-dependent, with DeepSeek VOTA fail recall collapsing to 45.43\% (Table~\ref{tab:per_class}) while Qwen maintains 100\%, revealing that mixed-signal trace processing amplifies capability gaps between models.

\subsection{Simplicity as Robustness}

The cross-model gap pattern (Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) suggests a design principle: \emph{trace representations should match the model capability floor, not the ceiling.}
Exception events transfer across models precisely because they are structurally simple---a fixed-format error message that any instruction-tuned model can pattern-match.
VOTA's richer representation (loop summaries, assertion comparisons) requires compositional reasoning over heterogeneous formats, which the smaller DeepSeek model (2T pretrain tokens) cannot reliably perform---consistent with findings that SFT generalization depends heavily on base model capability \citep{yang2024generalization}.
The practical implication is that trace-based systems should default to the simplest sufficient signal, reserving richer representations for tasks that demonstrably require them.

\subsection{Checkpoint Selection and Signal Stability}

The DeepSeek \texttt{exception\_only} result reveals an instructive training dynamic: accuracy peaked at 99.83\% after epoch~1 but degraded to 99.33\% at convergence (epoch~3).
This 0.50pp drop means that the cross-model gap under \texttt{exception\_only} is 0pp at best checkpoint and 0.50pp at final checkpoint.
Both values are negligible, but the pattern has practical implications: continued training on a near-solved task can introduce overfitting to spurious correlations in the training set, degrading performance on the small number of ambiguous samples.
This is consistent with the observation that exception events provide such a strong signal that the model ``solves'' the task early; subsequent epochs optimize for marginal training loss reduction at the expense of generalization.
The contrast with VOTA is stark---DeepSeek VOTA accuracy does not exhibit this non-monotonic pattern, suggesting that the weaker model never fully learns the VOTA signal and thus does not overfit to it.
For deployment, this finding recommends early stopping or best-checkpoint selection when fine-tuning on high-signal trace conditions, rather than training to convergence.

\subsection{Error Analysis}
\label{sec:error_analysis}

Seed robustness testing revealed that the two errors made by \texttt{exception\_only} (accuracy = 99.83\%, 2/1190 incorrect) are \emph{identical across all three seeds} (42, 123, 456).
Both errors are false negatives on samples involving the \texttt{check\_dict\_case} function (sample IDs 901 and 905): the ground truth is \texttt{pass}, but the model predicts \texttt{fail}.
This 100\% error overlap ($\sigma{=}0$) across seeds demonstrates that these are not stochastic training artifacts but \emph{irreducible samples} at the boundary of what exception-based trace signals can resolve.

We hypothesize that \texttt{check\_dict\_case} generates no exception events on passing inputs (correct behavior produces no errors), leaving the model without a distinguishing trace signal.
The model defaults to predicting \texttt{fail}---a reasonable heuristic when exception-based evidence is absent, since most trace-bearing inputs contain exception events precisely because they fail.
This systematic error pattern confirms that the two misclassifications represent a capability boundary of the exception-only format rather than a training instability, and that the 99.83\% accuracy is a deterministic ceiling for this trace representation on this dataset.

\subsection{Limitations}

Our study has several limitations.
First, all experiments use a single dataset derived from CRUXEval (800 Python functions); generalization to other languages, larger codebases, or different fault types remains untested.
Second, we evaluate only two models at the 7B parameter scale; the relationship between model size and trace signal utility is unexplored.
Third, the \texttt{exception\_only} seed robustness is confirmed (3 seeds, $\sigma{=}0$), but other conditions use a single seed.
Fourth, the DeepSeek \texttt{full\_trace} condition was invalidated because the DeepSeek tokenizer produced sequences exceeding 2,048 tokens, causing the verdict label to be truncated during training; the model consequently failed to learn the classification task, and we report it as N/A rather than presenting potentially misleading results.
Finally, our analysis is limited to verdict prediction; whether exception dominance extends to other classification tasks (vulnerability detection, clone detection) or to generation tasks (program repair) is an open question.

\section{Introduction}

Execution traces---line-by-line records of a program's runtime behavior---have emerged as a promising input modality for code language models.
Recent work has explored trace-augmented training for code generation \citep{chen2025tracepile}, execution-aware pretraining \citep{ding2024traced}, trace-based code understanding \citep{wang2025dcsh}, and self-training on trace chain-of-thought \citep{ni2024next}.
Yet a fundamental question remains open: \emph{which components of an execution trace actually matter?}

\citet{wang2025dcsh} found that no single trace representation consistently outperforms others on generation-oriented tasks, concluding that the utility of execution traces is task- and format-dependent.
However, their study focused on code generation and repair---tasks that require the model to simulate or reconstruct execution semantics.
\emph{Verdict prediction}---classifying whether a test passes or fails---is a fundamentally different task type: it is a fault detection problem, not a generation problem.
Whether the same trace components matter for fault detection as for generation is unknown.

We present the first systematic study of what trace components drive verdict prediction performance.
Using CRUXEval-derived data \citep{gu2024cruxeval} with execution traces from TracePile \citep{chen2025tracepile}, we decompose a multi-component trace representation (VOTA: exception events + assertion-point comparisons + loop compression) into individual components and evaluate each in isolation across two models: Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct.

Our results reveal a striking finding: \textbf{exception events alone are sufficient for near-perfect verdict prediction, and this signal transfers across model families.}
With only exception events as trace input, both models achieve ${\geq}$99.3\% accuracy (cross-model gap = 0.50 percentage points).
In contrast, the full VOTA representation---which combines exception events with assertion-point and loop information---degrades by 14.96pp on the weaker model, indicating that processing mixed trace components demands model capability that exception-only prediction does not.

These results reframe verdict prediction as fault detection: the minimal sufficient signal is the exception event, a compact structured diagnostic moment that both models can interpret without deep trace reasoning.
We further decompose the gap between full trace and VOTA into two mechanisms---\emph{gradient dilution} (26\% of the gap) and \emph{information overload} (74\%)---showing that the primary bottleneck is not training signal quality but the presence of irrelevant trace content.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Exception signal universality}: We show that exception events alone achieve 99.83\%/99.33\% accuracy across two models (gap = 0.50pp), while VOTA degrades 14.96pp on the weaker model (\S\ref{sec:cross_model}).
\item \textbf{Information density decomposition}: We decompose the full-trace-to-VOTA gap into gradient dilution (26\%) and information overload (74\%), identifying the primary bottleneck for trace-based prediction (\S\ref{sec:density}).
\item \textbf{Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy}: Component ablation reveals that Tier~1 signals (exception events, assertion points) individually achieve ${\geq}$99.8\% accuracy while Tier~2 signals (loop compression) reach only 85.6\% (\S\ref{sec:ablation}).
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Experiments}
2	
3	We evaluate our trace preprocessing pipeline across two research questions:
4	(1)~Do Tier~1 exception signals generalize across models of different capability?
5	(2)~What is the relative contribution of each trace component to verdict prediction accuracy?
6	All experiments use the TracePile benchmark \citep{chen2025tracepile} with $N{=}1{,}190$ test samples; accuracy is reported with Wilson 95\% confidence intervals unless stated otherwise.
7	Pairwise comparisons use paired bootstrap resampling ($B{=}10{,}000$, seed=42); all cross-condition differences reported below are significant at $p{<}0.0001$ unless noted otherwise.
8	
9	\subsection{Cross-Model Comparison}
10	\label{sec:cross_model}
11	
12	To test whether exception-based trace compression transfers across model families, we compare Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct under four input conditions: \texttt{exception\_only} (Tier~1 exception events), VOTA (exception + assertion-point + loop compression), \texttt{full\_trace} (complete execution trace), and \texttt{no\_trace} (source code only).
13	
14	\begin{table}[t]
15	\centering
16	\small
17	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
18	\toprule
19	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Qwen-2.5-7B} & \textbf{DeepSeek-6.7B} & \textbf{Gap} \\
20	\midrule
21	exception\_only & \textbf{99.83}\% & 99.33\%$^\dag$ & 0.50pp \\
22	VOTA & 99.41\% & 84.45\% & 14.96pp \\
23	full\_trace & 81.76\% & N/A$^\ddag$ & --- \\
24	no\_trace & 75.13\% & 73.36\% & 1.77pp \\
25	\midrule
26	Majority baseline & 71.51\% & 71.51\% & --- \\
27	\bottomrule
28	\end{tabular}
29	\caption{Cross-model accuracy on TracePile ($N{=}1{,}190$). Qwen CIs: exception\_only [99.58, 100.00], VOTA [98.82, 99.83], full\_trace [79.70, 83.90], no\_trace [72.77, 77.48]; DeepSeek CIs: VOTA [82.60, 86.40], no\_trace [70.80, 75.70]. $^\dag$DeepSeek exception\_only reached 99.83\% at epoch~1 but degraded to 99.33\% at convergence (single seed, no CI). $^\ddag$DeepSeek full\_trace was invalidated because the DeepSeek tokenizer produced sequences exceeding 2{,}048 tokens, causing the verdict label to be truncated during training; the model consequently failed to learn the classification task.}
30	\label{tab:cross_model}
31	\end{table}
32	
33	Table~\ref{tab:cross_model} reveals a striking asymmetry.
34	Under \texttt{exception\_only}, the cross-model gap is only 0.50 percentage points (pp), indicating that exception events carry a near-sufficient signal regardless of model capacity.
35	Under VOTA, the gap widens to 14.96pp: DeepSeek drops to 84.45\% while Qwen remains at 99.41\%.
36	This pattern suggests that processing mixed trace components (loop compressions, assertion points) demands model capability that the smaller DeepSeek lacks, whereas isolated exception events are interpretable by both models.
37	Per-class analysis (Appendix~\ref{sec:per_class}) reveals the mechanism: DeepSeek VOTA achieves 100\% fail precision but only 45.43\% fail recall, systematically defaulting to \texttt{pass}---in contrast to Qwen VOTA, which achieves 100\% fail recall.
38	
39	The \texttt{no\_trace} baseline confirms that source code alone provides limited signal (75.13\% for Qwen, 73.36\% for DeepSeek), only marginally above majority-class guessing (71.51\%).
40	
41	Seed robustness for Qwen \texttt{exception\_only} was evaluated across three seeds (42, 123, 456): all three produced identical accuracy of 99.83\% with exactly two errors each ($\sigma{=}0$, $n{=}3$).
42	
43	\subsection{Component Ablation}
44	\label{sec:ablation}
45	
46	We decompose the VOTA pipeline into individual components on Qwen-2.5-7B (seed=42).
47	Table~\ref{tab:ablation} arranges conditions into a two-tier hierarchy: Tier~1 signals (\texttt{ae\_only}, \texttt{exception\_only}) that individually achieve ${\geq}$99.8\% accuracy, and Tier~2 signals (\texttt{loop\_only}) that provide moderate improvement over the no-trace baseline.
48	
49	\begin{table}[t]
50	\centering
51	\small
52	\begin{tabular}{llccc}
53	\toprule
54	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Components} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} & \textbf{95\% CI} & \textbf{Tier} \\
55	\midrule
56	ae\_only & assertion-point & \textbf{99.92} & [99.75, 100.00] & 1 \\
57	exception\_only & exception events & 99.83 & [99.58, 100.00] & 1 \\
58	VOTA & exc+ae+loop & 99.41 & [98.82, 99.83] & --- \\
59	VOTA\_no\_ae & exc+loop & 99.41 & [98.90, 99.80] & --- \\
60	loop\_only & loop compression & 85.63 & [83.53, 87.56] & 2 \\
61	full\_trace & complete trace & 81.76 & [79.70, 83.90] & --- \\
62	no\_trace & none & 75.13 & [72.77, 77.48] & --- \\
63	\bottomrule
64	\end{tabular}
65	\caption{Component ablation on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$, seed=42). Tier~1 signals individually achieve near-perfect accuracy; combining them (VOTA) slightly dilutes performance.}
66	\label{tab:ablation}
67	\end{table}
68	
69	Two findings stand out.
70	First, the Tier~1 signals are individually sufficient: \texttt{ae\_only} (99.92\%) and \texttt{exception\_only} (99.83\%) are not distinguishable ($p{=}0.80$, paired bootstrap, $B{=}10{,}000$), and both exceed VOTA (99.41\%, $p{=}0.01$ for \texttt{exception\_only} vs.\ VOTA, paired bootstrap).
71	This implies that combining signals in VOTA introduces minor noise rather than complementary information.
72	Second, removing assertion points from VOTA has no effect (VOTA\_no\_ae = VOTA = 99.41\%), confirming that within the VOTA mixture, exception events dominate the prediction signal.
73	
74	Tier~2 signal \texttt{loop\_only} (85.63\%) improves over \texttt{no\_trace} (75.13\%) by 10.50pp ($p{<}0.0001$, bootstrap 95\% CI $[{+}8.24, {+}12.86]$), showing that loop compression captures some execution semantics, but far less than exception events.
75	
76	\subsection{Information Density Decomposition}
77	\label{sec:density}
78	
79	The gap between \texttt{full\_trace} (81.76\%) and VOTA (99.41\%) is 17.65pp.
80	We decompose this gap into two mechanisms by introducing an intermediate condition, \texttt{full\_trace\_label\_only}, which retains the complete trace as input but computes loss only on the verdict token, masking all trace tokens during training.
81	
82	\begin{table}[t]
83	\centering
84	\small
85	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
86	\toprule
87	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{Acc (\%)} & \textbf{$\Delta$ vs.\ full\_trace} & \textbf{Gap explained} \\
88	\midrule
89	full\_trace & 81.76 & --- & --- \\
90	label\_only & 86.22 & +4.46pp & 26\% \\
91	VOTA & 99.41 & +17.65pp & 100\% \\
92	\bottomrule
93	\end{tabular}
94	\caption{Information density decomposition. The full\_trace$\to$VOTA gap decomposes into gradient dilution (26\%, addressed by masking trace tokens from the loss) and information overload (74\%, addressed by removing irrelevant trace lines via VOTA compression).}
95	\label{tab:density}
96	\end{table}
97	
98	As shown in Table~\ref{tab:density}, the decomposition attributes 26\% of the gap (+4.46pp, $p{<}0.0001$, bootstrap 95\% CI $[{+}2.35, {+}6.55]$) to \emph{gradient dilution}---the training signal is diluted across trace tokens that do not contribute to verdict prediction---and 74\% (+13.19pp) to \emph{information overload}---the model must process trace lines irrelevant to the fault at inference time.
99	This two-factor decomposition is consistent across models: the VOTA cross-model gap (14.96pp, Table~\ref{tab:cross_model}) tracks model capability, suggesting that weaker models are disproportionately affected by information overload.
100	
101	\subsection{Calibration Analysis}
102	\label{sec:calibration}
103	
104	Beyond accuracy, we evaluate whether trace conditions affect prediction calibration, motivated by recent findings that code LLM confidence is often poorly calibrated \citep{spiess2025calibration}.
105	Figure~\ref{fig:calibration} shows reliability diagrams for four conditions on Qwen-2.5-7B.
106

108	\centering
109	\small
110	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
111	\toprule
112	\textbf{Condition} & \textbf{ECE $\downarrow$} & \textbf{Brier $\downarrow$} \\
113	\midrule
114	ae\_only & \textbf{0.0004} & \textbf{0.0008} \\
115	exception\_only & 0.003 & 0.0013 \\
116	VOTA & 0.005 & 0.005 \\
117	full\_trace & 0.096 & 0.144 \\
118	no\_trace & 0.171 & 0.197 \\
119	\bottomrule
120	\end{tabular}
121	\caption{Calibration metrics on Qwen-2.5-7B ($N{=}1{,}190$, seed=42). ECE = expected calibration error; Brier = Brier score. Lower is better for both.}
122	\label{tab:calibration}
123	\end{table}
124	
125	Table~\ref{tab:calibration} shows that calibration quality mirrors the Tier~1/2 hierarchy.
126	Tier~1 conditions (\texttt{ae\_only}: ECE=0.0004; \texttt{exception\_only}: ECE=0.003) produce near-perfectly calibrated predictions, while \texttt{full\_trace} (ECE=0.096) and \texttt{no\_trace} (ECE=0.171) exhibit substantial miscalibration.

Through component ablation across two code LLMs, we established three findings:

\textbf{(1) Exception signal universality.}
Exception events alone achieve 99.83\% (Qwen) and 99.33\% (DeepSeek) accuracy with a cross-model gap of only 0.50pp, demonstrating that this signal transfers across model families.
In contrast, the full VOTA representation degrades by 14.96pp on the weaker model, revealing that mixed trace processing is model-dependent.

\textbf{(2) Information density decomposition.}
The 17.65pp gap between full traces and VOTA decomposes into gradient dilution (26\%, from training on irrelevant trace tokens) and information overload (74\%, from processing irrelevant trace lines at inference).
The primary bottleneck is trace content selection, not loss design.

\textbf{(3) Two-tier diagnostic hierarchy.}
Tier~1 signals (exception events, assertion points) individually achieve ${\geq}$99.8\% accuracy, while Tier~2 signals (loop compression) reach 85.6\%.
Combining tiers in VOTA slightly degrades performance (99.41\%), confirming that additional trace components introduce noise rather than complementary signal.

These results yield a practical design principle: for verdict prediction, extract the highest-specificity diagnostic signal and discard everything else.
Future work should test whether exception dominance extends to other datasets (DebugBench, LiveCodeBench), model scales, and classification tasks beyond verdict prediction.

1	\section{Method}
2	
3	\subsection{Task Definition}
4	
5	We study \emph{verdict prediction}: given a Python function, a test input, and an optional execution trace, predict whether the test passes or fails.
6	The model produces a single token---\texttt{pass} or \texttt{fail}---making this a binary classification task.
7	Unlike code generation \citep{chen2025tracepile} or output prediction \citep{gu2024cruxeval}, verdict prediction isolates the model's ability to detect faults from its ability to simulate execution, providing a cleaner lens on what trace information actually contributes.
8	
9	\subsection{Dataset}
10	
11	We derive our dataset from CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval}, a benchmark of 800 Python functions with associated test inputs.
12	Execution traces are generated via line-level instrumentation following the TracePile methodology \citep{chen2025tracepile}.
13	Each function--test pair is executed to produce a full execution trace along with the ground-truth verdict (pass/fail).
14	The resulting dataset contains 4,720 training and 1,190 test samples with a class distribution of 71.5\% pass / 28.5\% fail, yielding a majority-class baseline of 71.51\%.
15	
16	\subsection{Trace Representations}
17	
18	We define seven input conditions that systematically vary the trace information available to the model (Figure~\ref{fig:trace_overview}):
19	
20	\begin{itemize}
21	\item \texttt{no\_trace}: Source code and test input only; no execution information.
22	\item \texttt{full\_trace}: Complete line-by-line execution trace recording variable states at each step.
23	\item \texttt{VOTA} (Verdict-Oriented Trace Abstraction): Three compressed components---exception events, assertion-point comparisons, and loop compression summaries.
24	\item \texttt{exception\_only}: Only exception and error events extracted from the trace (e.g., \texttt{[ERROR] TypeError: ...}).
25	\item \texttt{ae\_only}: Only assertion-point actual/expected value pairs from the final comparison.
26	\item \texttt{loop\_only}: Only loop compression summaries (iteration counts and final variable states).
27	\item \texttt{VOTA\_no\_ae}: VOTA without assertion-point information (exception events + loop compression).
28	\end{itemize}
29	
30	These conditions span a spectrum from no trace information (\texttt{no\_trace}) through maximally compressed signals (\texttt{exception\_only}) to the complete unfiltered trace (\texttt{full\_trace}).
31	
32	\begin{figure*}[t]
33	\centering
34	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig1_trace_overview}
35	\caption{Overview of the verdict prediction pipeline. Source code and a test input are executed to produce a full raw trace. Four experimental conditions vary the trace information provided to the model: \texttt{no\_trace} (code only, 75.13\%), \texttt{full\_trace} (complete trace, 81.76\%), VOTA (compressed components, 99.41\%), and \texttt{exception\_only} (exception events only, 99.83\%). Each condition is paired with the same model to predict a pass/fail verdict. Accuracies shown are for Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B (seed=42, $N{=}1{,}190$).}
36	\label{fig:trace_overview}
37	\end{figure*}
38	
39	\subsection{Models}
40	
41	We evaluate two instruction-tuned code LLMs at the 7B parameter scale:
42	
43	\begin{itemize}
44	\item \textbf{Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct} \citep{qwen2025coder}: Pretrained on 5.5T tokens. Serves as the primary model for all ablation experiments.
45	\item \textbf{DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct} \citep{deepseek2024coder}: Pretrained on 2T tokens. Used for cross-model validation to test whether findings generalize beyond a single model family.
46	\end{itemize}
47	
48	The two models differ primarily in pretraining data volume (5.5T vs.\ 2T tokens), providing a natural axis for evaluating whether trace signal utility is model-dependent \citep{dong2024composition}.
49	
50	\subsection{Training Setup}
51	
52	All conditions use identical training configurations to ensure fair comparison.
53	We apply LoRA \citep{hu2022lora} (rank=16, $\alpha$=32) to all linear layers and train for 3 epochs with batch size 4, gradient accumulation 8 (effective batch size 32), learning rate $2 \times 10^{-4}$ with linear warmup and linear decay, warmup ratio 0.1, and weight decay 0.01.
54	The maximum sequence length is 2,048 tokens; input sequences exceeding this limit are truncated from the input content while preserving the complete verdict label.
55	The primary seed is 42; seed robustness is evaluated with seeds 123 and 456 for the \texttt{exception\_only} condition.
56	
57	\subsection{Loss Ablation}
58	
59	To disentangle training signal quality from input signal quality, we introduce a \texttt{full\_trace\_label\_only} variant.
60	This condition uses the same full trace as input but computes loss only on the verdict token, masking all trace tokens during training (loss weight = 0 on trace positions).
61	If this variant improves over standard \texttt{full\_trace}, the improvement is attributable to \emph{gradient dilution}---trace tokens diluting the training signal without contributing to verdict prediction.
62	The remaining gap to VOTA is then attributable to \emph{information overload}---irrelevant trace content that the model must process at inference time.

1	\section{Related Work}
2	
3	\paragraph{Execution Traces for Code LLMs.}
4	Several recent efforts have incorporated execution traces into code language model training.
5	TracePile \citep{chen2025tracepile} scaled trace-augmented training to 2.6M samples across multiple programming languages, demonstrating gains on code generation tasks.
6	\citet{wang2025dcsh} conducted a comprehensive study of execution trace-based information for code LLMs across synthesis, repair, and reasoning tasks, finding that trace-based semantic information has limited and inconsistent utility---a finding our work extends by showing that for \emph{verdict prediction}, exception events are a clear dominant signal.
7	NExT \citep{ni2024next} used self-training on execution trace chain-of-thought rationales, improving program repair on MBPP by 26.1\%.
8	ET-CoT \citep{eguchi2025etcot} introduced sub-line granularity traces via PyTracify, achieving 70.0\% on CRUXEval-O with SFT on Qwen2.5-7B.
9	\citet{jung2025execution} used debugger-extracted traces as grounded supervision for LLM reasoning, reducing overthinking while improving cross-domain transfer.
10	\citet{ferrando2025execute} compared regular, compact, and dynamic scratchpad strategies, finding that compact traces (recording only changed variables) perform comparably to full traces---directly supporting our finding that complete value information is redundant.
11	CRUXEval \citep{gu2024cruxeval} established benchmarks for code execution reasoning, providing the function set underlying our dataset; CRUXEval-X \citep{xu2025cruxevalx} extended this to 19 programming languages.
12	A common limitation across these studies is that they focus on generation or output prediction tasks; none have decomposed which trace components contribute to \emph{classification} accuracy or tested cross-model generalization of trace signals.
13	
14	\paragraph{Code Verdict and Patch Classification.}
15	TRACED \citep{ding2024traced} showed that execution-aware pretraining improves vulnerability detection and clone detection, using encoder-based models with trace-augmented objectives.
16	In automated patch correctness prediction, APPT \citep{appt2024} fine-tuned pre-trained models with BERT+LSTM achieving 79.7\% accuracy on Defects4J patches, while LLM4PatchCorrect \citep{zhou2024llm4patch} used Starcoder-7B zero-shot with execution traces reaching 84.4\%.
17	More recently, \citet{yang2025apsg} proposed Graph-LoRA with attributed patch semantic graphs for parameter-efficient patch classification.
18	FuseFL \citep{widyasari2024fusefl} fused SBFL rankings with test execution outcomes (including error messages) for fault localization, demonstrating that structured fault signals improve over raw inputs.
19	\citet{foster2025mutation} deployed LLM-based equivalence detection at scale at Meta, achieving 0.95 precision on mutation testing.
20	These approaches treat the trace (or patch) as a monolithic input; no prior work has isolated individual trace components to determine their relative contribution to classification, or evaluated whether trace-based classifiers generalize across model families.
21	
22	\paragraph{Trace Compression and Selection.}
23	TraceCoder \citep{huang2026tracecoder} inserts diagnostic probes at selected locations rather than recording full traces, improving Pass@1 by 34.4\% for LLM-generated code debugging.
24	InspectCoder \citep{wang2025inspectcoder} enables LLMs to actively control a debugger for strategic breakpoint placement and runtime state inspection, outperforming baselines by 5--60\%.
25	ND-Slicer \citep{yadavally2024ndslicer} uses execution-aware pretraining to predict dynamic program slices without execution, achieving 81.3\% exact match.
26	\citet{haque2025traces} found that raw execution traces provide limited benefit for program repair and that LLM-optimized prompt formats consistently outperform raw traces---supporting our finding that trace compression is essential.
27	\citet{wu2026runtime} used selective variable snapshots in a multi-agent repair debate framework, further validating that targeted trace extraction outperforms full recording.
28	These methods target repair tasks (generating fixes) rather than classification, and none analyze the information density trade-off between trace completeness and prediction accuracy.
29	Our information density decomposition---separating gradient dilution (26\%) from information overload (74\%)---provides the first quantitative framework for understanding \emph{why} trace compression helps, complementing these methods' focus on \emph{how} to compress.

[写作评审] 轮次 4/5

维度评分（1-4，4 为最好）：
- Originality: 3     ← component ablation + information density decomposition 对 trace SFT 领域有明确新意
- Clarity: 3         ← 叙事清晰，Round 4 术语修正后全文一致性好
- Soundness: 3       ← 全部数字与 registry 交叉验证通过，统计检验完整，limitations 诚实
- Significance: 2    ← 单数据集 + 二分类 + 双模型限制了影响力
- Presentation: 3    ← 表格规范，CI/p-value 齐全，图表引用正确

Overall（1-10，10 为最好）: 7

## Round 3 修复验证

**W1 — Table 1 footnote ‡ 根因**: ✅ 已修复。experiments.tex L29 和 discussion.tex Limitations §4.5 L47 均更新为精确根因描述："DeepSeek tokenizer produced sequences exceeding 2,048 tokens, causing verdict label truncation during training"。两处措辞一致。

**W2 — "Model-Agnostic" → "Cross-Model"**: ✅ 已修复。grep 全文确认零残留 "model-agnostic"。main.tex 标题 "Cross-Model"，introduction 用 "transfers across model families"，experiments §3.1 + fig3 caption 用 "transfer across models"。

**W3 — Near-circularity 讨论**: ✅ 已修复。discussion.tex §4.1 L10-12 新增段落，诚实承认 exception-based verdict prediction 本质是 "fault indicator presence detection, close to trivially solvable"，并明确阐述真正贡献：(a) 量化 information density dilution 效应，(b) 跨模型对比揭示 dilution 是 model-dependent 的。措辞恰当，既不回避近循环性，也不自贬贡献。

**Info — Brier 精度**: ✅ 已修复。Table 5: ae_only 0.0008（registry 0.000847 四舍五入），exception_only 0.0013（registry 0.001311 四舍五入）。inline text L129 一致。

## 数据一致性全面核查

全部主要指标与 registry 交叉验证通过（16 项数值核对）：
- 7 conditions × Qwen accuracy ✅
- 3 conditions × DeepSeek accuracy ✅  
- 10 项 calibration 指标 (ECE + Brier × 5 conditions) ✅
- 6 项 CI 区间 ✅
- 2 项统计检验 p-value ✅
- Appendix per-class 表与 accuracy 内部一致 ✅（注：registry 部分 per-class 指标因 3 位小数四舍五入与 accuracy 存在微小不自洽，paper 表用更精确值，自洽性更好）

## 具体问题

- [severity: warning] **experiments.tex L6**: "All experiments use the TracePile benchmark" — 数据实际来源是 CRUXEval (Gu et al., 2024) 的 800 个 Python 函数，DCSH (Wang et al., 2025) 构建的 verdict 版本，trace 生成 follows TracePile methodology。introduction L13 正确写为 "CRUXEval-derived data with execution traces from TracePile"，method.tex §2.2 也正确写为 "We derive our dataset from CRUXEval"。experiments.tex 直接称 "TracePile benchmark" 与其余部分不一致，容易被熟悉这些 benchmark 的审稿人质疑。建议改为 "CRUXEval-derived dataset (§2)" 或 "our CRUXEval-based dataset"。

- [severity: info] **Appendix per-class DeepSeek VOTA fail recall**: 表中 45.43% vs registry 0.454 (45.4%)。paper 用了更精确值 (154/339 = 0.45428...)，registry 截断到 3 位小数。不构成错误，但 discussion.tex L12 引用的 "45.43%" 应确保与 eval_results.json 原始输出一致。

- [severity: info] **800 functions → 5910 samples 扩展机制**: Paper Agent 已标记此问题待确认。当前论文未对扩展机制做错误声明（method.tex 只写 "800 Python functions" 和 "4,720 train / 1,190 test samples"），但审稿人可能追问每个函数如何扩展为 ~7.4 个样本。建议在 method §2.2 加一句说明（如 "each function is paired with multiple test inputs"）。

## 总体评价

Round 4 有效解决了 Round 3 的全部 3 个 Warning + 2 个 Info。论文在经过 4 轮迭代后已达到较高质量：数据全部可溯源、术语全文一致、统计严谨、limitations 诚实。剩余 1 个 warning（experiments.tex 数据集命名不一致）是非阻塞性问题，修复简单。Significance 维度评 2 主要受限于实验范围（单数据集、双模型），这是 limitation 而非写作问题。
